title: The US-R1-001 bullet cites `scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt sections 4-5` as it…
description:
The US-R1-001 bullet cites `scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt sections 4-5` as its evidence pointer, but that file is ephemeral and gitignored (.gitignore:81) and is overwritten by every subsequent review round; it is not tracked on main. patterns.md is by contract durable and versioned on main, so this cross-reference is unresolvable for any future reader. The bullet already states the measured facts inline ('measured: two criteria in US-001's own acceptanceCriteria, patterns.md keyword-density and CLAUDE.md placement, both did this against unmodified main'), so the citation is supplementary rather than load-bearing. Consider dropping the pointer or replacing it with the CAM issue number, which is durable.

Source: cam/issue-372
Review round: 2

suggestion-fingerprint: 7155ce033e6c

spec.scope:
Close out the authoring/knowledge-surface defects left open by CAM-372, whose two bullets shipped to scripts/cam/patterns.md at lines 899 and 901 in commit bf01bd23 (PR #300, v0.224.0). Three folded issues, one PR, doc-and-test-only, NO binary rebuild (the sidecar executes none of this).

(1) CAM-376, the lead issue and a defect in content the previous cycle itself shipped. The bullet at patterns.md:901 ends its measured-facts parenthetical with the bare-prose citation 'see scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt sections 4-5'. That path is gitignored at .gitignore:81, is untracked, does not exist on main (git show main:<path> exits 128), and is overwritten by every subsequent review round. patterns.md is by contract durable and versioned on main, so a future reader can never resolve the pointer. Worse, the bullet was authored in direct violation of a rule already sitting ~150 lines above it in the same file: lines 742/748 govern exactly which ephemeral artifacts may be named and on what terms. Replace the dangling pointer with a durable reference to the review round that produced the evidence. The bullet already states the measured facts inline, so the citation is supplementary, not load-bearing: nothing is lost by making it resolvable.

(2) CAM-377, folded in because it lands in the same file and the same authoring rule-set. Grounding established the gap is total: no bullet anywhere in patterns.md states that an acceptance criterion pinning a main-derived number should DERIVE it (git show main:FILE | wc -l) rather than freeze a literal. Line 899 covers proving an oracle goes red; it says nothing about how the comparand is obtained. The two ideas are adjacent but disjoint. The concrete instance that raised this (CAM-372's criterion 2 hardcoding 897) is moot, that PRD merged and will never run again, so ONLY the generalizable rule survives and is worth shipping. Append it as a new top-level bullet at EOF.

(3) CAM-374, folded in because it is the worked example the CAM-372 rule at patterns.md:899 explicitly cites by issue number. Fixing it closes the loop that rule opened. The assertion at test/dispatch.test.ts:754, expect(recordedSleeps.every((ms) => ms <= 1_000)).toBe(true), is non-falsifiable in isolation: the test overrides pollIntervalMs to 1_000 but never passes retryBaseMs, so the un-overridden default of 300 (src/tmux/dispatch.ts:544) means a first-retry computeBackoffMs value of roughly 300-600 ms would slip under the 1000 ms bound and the assertion would still pass. Its stated intent, 'zero backoff sleeps', is therefore unenforced. The adjacent geometrySamplerCalls === 0 assertion at line 755 is airtight and independently satisfies the acceptance criterion, so this is a strengthening, not a bug fix: the enclosing test's behavior must not change and it must still pass.

OUT OF SCOPE: do not touch the other three review-artifact mentions at patterns.md:224, :742 and :748. Those name the path while discussing its ephemerality and its gate-allowlisting mechanics, which is self-consistent and correct. Only line 901 cites it as evidence a reader is expected to go read. Do not edit the bullet at patterns.md:899. Do not touch src/tmux/dispatch.ts: the retryBaseMs default of 300 is correct and this story changes test assertions only.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1 (CAM-376) RED-ON-MAIN, swept verbatim by the orchestrator against a git show main: temp tree, exit 1 confirmed. The self-nullifying-oracle bullet no longer cites the ephemeral artifact: `L=$(grep -n 'self-nullifying-oracle subspecies' scripts/cam/patterns.md | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); test -n "$L" && ! sed -n "${L}p" scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -q 'review-artifact'`. The `test -n "$L"` guard is mandatory and fail-closed: without it an empty L makes `sed -n "p"` print the entire file, which is the exact defect this same bullet documents.

AC2 (CAM-376) RED-ON-MAIN, swept verbatim, main count is 4. The total number of lines in patterns.md mentioning review-artifact drops from 4 to exactly 3, proving the three legitimate mentions at :224/:742/:748 survive untouched and only the evidence-citation was removed: `test "$(grep -c 'review-artifact' scripts/cam/patterns.md)" -eq 3`.

AC3 (CAM-376) The replacement pointer is durable, i.e. resolvable from main alone with no ephemeral path. The edited bullet must retain its inline measured-facts clause and point at the durable review round instead of the artifact file. Verify no gitignored path remains anywhere in the edited bullet: extract the bullet line, and for every `scripts/cam/*` or `.claude/*` path token it contains, `git check-ignore -q <token>` must exit non-zero. Report the before/after text of the bullet verbatim in handoff.json.

AC4 (CAM-377) RED-ON-MAIN, swept verbatim, zero matches on main. A new top-level bullet exists stating the derive-don't-freeze rule for main-derived comparands in acceptance criteria, and it names the concrete idiom: `grep -qE 'git show main:[^ ]*\|[[:space:]]*wc -l' scripts/cam/patterns.md`. The bullet must carry the standard provenance suffix naming CAM-377 and today's date, and must explicitly distinguish itself from the falsifiability rule at patterns.md:899 (899 = prove the oracle can go red; this one = do not freeze the comparand it compares against).

AC5 (CAM-377) PINNING ORACLE, deliberately GREEN on main, labelled as such per the rule at patterns.md:899. This guards the append-at-EOF convention: many bullets cross-reference each other by absolute line number, so any mid-file insert silently rots them. Lines 1 through 898 of patterns.md must remain byte-identical to main: `diff <(git show main:scripts/cam/patterns.md | head -898) <(head -898 scripts/cam/patterns.md)` exits 0. Line 899 is excluded from the range only because it is the boundary; it must also be unmodified, assert that separately.
AC6 (CAM-374) RED-ON-MAIN, swept verbatim, the string is present at test/dispatch.test.ts:754 on main. The non-falsifiable bound is gone: `! grep -q 'ms <= 1_000' test/dispatch.test.ts`.

AC7 (CAM-374) The replacement assertion is provably falsifiable, and the implementer must MEASURE this rather than argue it. Demonstrate redness by a temporary local mutation: pass `retryBaseMs` explicitly, or otherwise inject a single backoff-shaped sleep value into recordedSleeps, and confirm the NEW assertion FAILS where the old `<= 1_000` bound PASSED. Revert the mutation before committing. Record the exact mutation used, the old-assertion result and the new-assertion result verbatim in handoff.json under officialDocsValidated or a sibling field. An assertion that cannot be shown to fail under this mutation does not satisfy this criterion.

AC8 (CAM-374) PINNING, expected green: the enclosing test at test/dispatch.test.ts:700-765 still passes unchanged in behavior, and the airtight `expect(geometrySamplerCalls).toBe(0)` assertion at line 755 is retained, not deleted. `bun test test/dispatch.test.ts` exits 0.

AC9 Full quality spine green: `bun run typecheck` zero errors, `bun test` with a pass count at or above main's 5192 baseline and 0 fail, and `bun run check:all` green. A doc-and-test-only diff that removes no test must not lower the pass count.
gotchas: patterns.md has NO SECTIONS. It is one `# Codebase Patterns` heading, a ~6-line preamble, then a FLAT blank-line-separated list of top-level `- ` bullets to EOF (901 lines on main). scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md and .claude/agents/subagent-planner.md both instruct you to grep it 'for the section'; that is a fiction. Discovery is pure keyword grep, so a new bullet is findable ONLY by its own keywords. Choose keywords deliberately.

APPEND-AT-EOF is mandatory. Bullets cross-reference each other by absolute line number (patterns.md:899 alone cites :566, :570, :572, :772, :774, :776). A mid-file insert silently rots every one of them. This is what AC5 guards.

The CAM-376 edit is an IN-PLACE edit of line 901, the file's final line. Keep it a single physical line: every bullet in this file is one long physical line, and splitting it would break the flat-bullet parse convention and shift line numbering.
Never prefix a living rule with `[resolved YYYY-MM]`. That marker means an already-resolved one-time mechanic, and `cam patterns archive` sweeps any bullet carrying it into patterns.archive.md.

`git ls-files <path>` exits 0 even on no match, so its exit status is a useless discriminator for trackedness. Use `git ls-files --error-unmatch <path>` (exits 1 when untracked) or assert empty stdout. `git show main:<path>` exits 128 for an untracked path.

scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt DOES currently exist on disk (stale local copy from the last review round). Any oracle that merely reads the path will pass locally and fail on a clean checkout. Judge trackedness via git, never via the filesystem.

In test/dispatch.test.ts the literal 1_000 in the assertion is the same value as the `pollIntervalMs: 1_000` override on line 736. If the replacement assertion pins an exact poll-interval value, derive it from the override rather than re-freezing the literal, which is precisely the CAM-377 rule this same PR is shipping. Practice what the bullet preaches.

retryBaseMs = 300 and retryMaxMs = 2_000 are destructuring defaults inside sendKeysVerified's options bag (src/tmux/dispatch.ts:544-545), NOT named exported constants, so they cannot be imported into the test. pollIntervalMs = 200 is likewise a destructuring default (src/tmux/dispatch.ts:538) and is overridden to 1_000 by this test.
The test uses a fake clock: Date.now is monkeypatched and advanced only by the injected sleepFn, restored in a finally block. Do not disturb that idiom.
NO REBUILD. The diff touches docs and one test file; the sidecar executes neither, so the coherence-skip rule applies and the binary correctly stays behind main.
No file-size budget covers .md and none can: scripts/check-file-sizes.ts globs {src,scripts,test}/**/*.{ts,tsx} only. test/dispatch.test.ts IS covered, but this change does not grow it materially.
domainTerms: oracle-falsifiability rule: every acceptance-criterion oracle and every in-test assertion must be proven RED against unmodified main via an exhaustive sweep, not a sample, before it is trusted. Shipped by CAM-372 at patterns.md:899.

pinning oracle: an acceptance-criterion oracle that is deliberately GREEN on main because it asserts invariance (that something did NOT change) rather than new behavior. Legitimate only when labelled inline as such, never laundered as red.

self-nullifying oracle: an oracle that returns GREEN exactly when its own anchor is absent, e.g. unguarded `sed -n "${L}p"` with empty L printing the whole file, or a `while read` loop over zero matches exiting 0 vacuously. Documented at patterns.md:901.

durable vs ephemeral artifact: durable means tracked and versioned on main (patterns.md, issue JSON, ADRs); ephemeral means gitignored or untracked per-cycle state (review-artifact.txt, worker-report.json, prd.json, handoff.json). A durable file must never cite an ephemeral one as evidence.
append-at-EOF convention: new patterns.md bullets go at end of file, because existing bullets cross-reference one another by absolute line number.
